answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit bids, with voting weight capped by the amount locked and rewards paid only after the work is independently verified. Splitting one stake among many identities does not increase total influence, while creating identities that matter requires buying and locking more tokens. The attacker pays the opportunity cost of frozen capital and risks losing it to slashing when fraud is proven. The inlet may be small, but a lantern of checks can expose claims before they reach the ocean of agents.
